extracted.intended_audience: natural philosophers, experimental scientists, and students of inductive method (readers of Baconian methodology)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for collecting and using experimental 'instances' (examples) and using seven modes of action to perform and interpret natural philosophy by induction, as set out in Bacon's Novum Organum. Emphasizes types of decisive instances (27 prerogative instances) and practical modes of manipulation/observation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuance (duration) as a mode of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Continuance (duration) of a body’s condition affects processes: conformations assumed by bodies left to themselves (e.g., mouldiness) are checked by heat; confinement impedes proper motion; continuance in an open vessel useful for separations, in a hermetically sealed for mixtures, and in a vessel partly closed but admitting air for putrefaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use duration and degree of confinement/ventilation as an experimental variable: open vessels to separate, sealed vessels to produce mixtures, partly closed to favor putrefaction. Note violent motion can result from confinement. Collect examples of effects of continuance from many quarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direction of motion (fifth mode of action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direction of motion: when a body meeting another arrests, repels, allows, or directs its original motion — often determined by the figure and position of vessels or by one body within another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider shape and orientation of apparatus (e.g., upright cone for condensation in alembics; reversed cone for sugar refining), use strainers and opposed bodies to allow part of a substance to pass and impede the rest, and exploit internal bodies (pebbles to collect muddy particles; egg white to glue grosser particles). Observe casting and modelling as examples. Treat vessel geometry and internal additives as deliberate experimental variables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harmony and aversion (sympathies and antipathies)
rubrics_metrics.description: Harmony (correspondence) and aversion (enmity) between bodies — occult or specific properties — reflect correspondences of form/conformation or of abundance/rarity; many putative sympathies/antipathies are errors or fables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate correspondences of substances (e.g., sulphur with oil/flame; mercury with water/air), the relation of metals/vegetables/animals in quantity vs form, and harmonies between bodies and their supports/menstruums (climate, soil, manure). Test grafting compatibilities, dietary compatibilities (carnivores vs herbs), and collect reliable agricultural, navigational, and medical reports on lunar/motion effects. Reject rash superstitious claims; focus on experimentally verified harmonies (e.g., magnet–iron, gold–quicksilver) and on 'occult' medicinal specificities only where supported by diligent inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternation and interchange (seventh mode of action)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternation/interchange of the other six modes of action: compound series or chains of alternating actions produce effects that are powerful but difficult to trace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that many phenomena result from a sequence or alternation of simpler modes; tracing such chains is hard and requires deeper investigation of the constituent modes before giving examples or practical application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative (solitary) instances — 'solitary instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Solitary instances are one of the prerogative instances that expedite the exclusive mode of arriving at the form and assist the understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use solitary instances to quickly indicate the true form or cause by an instance that isolates the property of interest. Collect and place them in synoptical tables as high-value evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'migrating instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Migrating instances are a named prerogative class of instances used in induction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are instances that 'migrate' through related natural classes and can help in recognizing common laws across gradations (useful in minerals, etc.). Collect for theory when forming synoptical tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'conspicuous (ostensive) instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Conspicuous (ostensive) instances visibly exhibit the property under investigation and help to confine and indicate the affirmative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ conspicuous examples that openly display the phenomenon; useful early in analysis to show presence/absence of a property.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'clandestine instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Clandestine instances are prerogative instances that elevate the understanding and lead toward general natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek hidden or indirect instances that reveal underlying commonalities; useful in advancing to more general concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'constitutive instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Constitutive instances are nearly as direct in elevating the understanding toward general natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use constitutive instances to approach general forms; collect these during the construction of synoptical tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'similar instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Similar instances are those showing resemblance among classes; they are less directly elevating than clandestine or singular instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect similar instances to indicate degrees of resemblance; these can be gathered immediately and help grouping in synoptical tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'singular instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Singular instances are particular cases that can elevate the understanding and are among the instances worth collecting immediately.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record striking single examples which may be highly informative; include them early in tables as they can outvalue many ordinary instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'deviating (deviating) instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Deviating instances correct the understanding of its habits by showing exceptions or deviations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use deviating instances to test and correct generalizations and habits of thought; collect them promptly to avoid false generalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'bordering instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Bordering instances lead to the grand form or fabric of the universe; they are of high value for theory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek instances at boundaries between kinds that suggest broader unifying forms; collect diligently for theory-building.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'instances of power'
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of power are those that show where practice should commence to avoid repeating the labors of others; they serve to point out practical beginnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these to identify promising starting points for experimental or practical work; collect them early to guide application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'accompanying and hostile instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Accompanying and hostile instances are prerogative classes that confine and indicate affirmative or negative relations between phenomena.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document instances that regularly accompany a phenomenon and those hostile to it; these help delimit causal relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'subjunctive instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Subjunctive instances are named prerogative instances that help confine and more immediately indicate the affirmative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use hypothetical or conditional instances (subjunctive) to test boundaries of causation and necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'instances of alliance'
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of alliance elevate the understanding toward general and common natures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect allied examples showing structural or functional kinship; they help in unifying concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'instances of the cross'
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of the cross guard the understanding from false forms and causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use crossing instances to challenge and disconfirm spurious causes; they operate as checks against error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'instances of divorce'
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of divorce guard the understanding from false forms and causes by separating conflated factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply instances that separate factors previously combined to reveal true causal contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'instances of the gate'
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of the gate are among those that should be collected immediately and serve as crucial points of access in inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify gateway instances that open a line of investigation; put them early in synoptical tables to guide further collection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'citing instances (instances of citation)'
rubrics_metrics.description: Citing instances (instances of citation) are named prerogative instances used in the method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use authoritative or well-documented cases as references to support or test hypotheses; include their provenance and conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'instances of the road' (instances of the course)
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of the road or course are prerogative instances that assist the investigator's progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect instances that indicate directionality or sequence in processes; useful for reconstructing chains of cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'supplementary instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Supplementary instances are additional instances that support or extend other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather supporting examples to reinforce emerging patterns; use them to test the robustness of inductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'lancing instances' (instances of piercing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Lancing instances (termed lancing instances) are among the prerogative classes used to penetrate problems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sharply revealing instances that 'pierce' a problem and expose its underlying nature; include them as high-value items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'instances of the rod'
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of the rod are listed among the prerogative instances as tools for measuring or guiding inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employ measuring or standardizing instances that can serve as a 'rod' or measure in experimentation (cf. mathematical instances that 'measure' practice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'instances of the course'
rubrics_metrics.description: Instances of the course refer to those indicating progression or sequence — used to measure practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect sequential/processual instances that allow one to quantify or measure stages of a phenomenon; mathematical instances are exemplar 'measures.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'doses of nature'
rubrics_metrics.description: Doses of nature are instances that help measure or scale natural operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instances that reveal proportionality or dosage effects (e.g., measure of motion, rate effects) to quantify natural laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'wrestling instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Wrestling instances are prerogative instances that exert or test opposing forces and effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use antagonistic or competitive instances to reveal causal dominance or resistance between factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'suggesting instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggesting instances induce us to aspire to what may be possible; they point practice toward possible aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect imaginative or suggestive examples that open avenues for practical pursuit; include early to guide inventive work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'generally useful instances'
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally useful instances are among those to be collected immediately and which assist both senses/understanding and furnish general practice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather broadly applicable examples that are useful across multiple inquiries; these form the practical backbone of applied work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prerogative instances — 'magical instances' (twenty-seventh)
rubrics_metrics.description: Magical instances are those where the efficient agent is scanty compared to the grandeur of the effect, producing seemingly miraculous results; they are produced (as conjectured) by (1) self-multiplication, (2) excitation/invitation of another substance, or (3) excess rapidity of one motion over another.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigate cases such as self-multiplying fire or poisons, magnet exciting needles, leaven, or gunpowder explosions. Study harmonies for the first two kinds and measures of motion for the third. Collect these sparingly but diligently; they elevate practice and may point to powerful principles. Be cautious about claims of per minima transformations — no clear indications yet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collection priority guidance for prerogative instances
rubrics_metrics.description: Some prerogative instances must be collected immediately, others after completing synoptical tables. Those to be collected immediately include similar, singular, deviating, bordering, instances of power, instances of the gate, suggesting, generally useful, and magical instances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assembling synoptical tables, prioritize the immediately collectible prerogative instances (listed above). Collect the remainder after more detailed investigation of properties; place prerogative instances prominently as they often outweigh many ordinary instances.

rubrics_metrics.name: How prerogative instances assist theory vs practice
rubrics_metrics.description: Prerogative instances excel ordinary instances with advantages that regard either theory or practice, or both: with regard to theory they assist the senses or the understanding (in various manners named); with regard to practice they point out, measure, or elevate it (instances of power point where to commence; suggesting instances induce aspiration; mathematical instances measure; generally useful and magical instances elevate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify collected instances by whether they primarily aid sensory access, understanding (form discovery), or practical application; use that classification to prioritize use in induction and in forming tables.
